newsitem.title: FRANCE: China's Qian due in Paris for business trip.
newsitem.headline: China's Qian due in Paris for business trip.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen arrives in Paris on Friday night for wide-ranging talks sealing a back-to-business partnership, the French foreign ministry said on Friday.

Qian, who is also vice-premier, was invited by French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette but he will start his visit by meeting President Jacques Chirac, an honour reflecting Paris's hopes of boosting trade with Beijing.
French foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said Qian's heavy agenda included preparing Chirac's state visit to China due this spring. He is due to leave on Sunday.

"(Both countries) share a determination to flesh out the partnership between us with a substantial and global dialogue," Rummelhardt said, adding that France's two percent share of the Chinese market was "still insufficient".

The spokesman added that relations between the two countries had recovered their normal footing since a joint communique published in January 1994 after a row over the sale by France of 60 Mirage fighters to Taiwan.

A diplomatic clash over human rights clouded Chinese Premier Li Peng's visit to Paris in April 1995 although the Chinese went ahead with signing contracts totalling 10 billion francs ($2 billion), mostly for 33 Airbus Industrie airliners.

France plans to send several ministers to China in the coming weeks including junior telecommunications minister Francois Fillon in late January and later junior foreign trade minister Yves Galland, Environment Minister Corinne Lepage and Defence Minister Charles Millon.
